front: What must every federal-court SMJ analysis begin with?
back: Federal courts have limited jurisdiction: Art. III + a statutory grant; SMJ cannot be waived or conferred by consent; raised any time (Rule 12(h)(3)).
Federal-question jurisdiction exists only if the federal issue appears in the plaintiff's own properly pleaded claim; anticipated federal defenses don't count (Mottley).

front: Four Grable/Gunn factors for a state claim with an embedded federal issue?
back: Federal issue (1) necessarily raised, (2) actually disputed, (3) substantial to the federal system, (4) resolvable federally without disrupting the federal–state balance.

Complete diversity (no plaintiff shares citizenship with any defendant) + amount in controversy exceeding $75,000 exclusive of interest and costs; measured at filing (§ 1332(a); Strawbridge; Grupo Dataflux).
No. The amount must EXCEED $75,000, exclusive of interest and costs.
Physical presence in a State + intent to remain indefinitely; one domicile at a time; old domicile continues until a new one is acquired.

front: Citizenship of a U.S. citizen domiciled abroad?
back: Stateless — cannot sue or be sued in diversity; destroys complete diversity (Newman-Green).

front: Lawful permanent resident alien domiciled in California v. California citizen — alienage jurisdiction?
back: No. § 1332(a)(2) excludes suits between a State citizen and a permanent-resident alien domiciled in the same State.
Every State/foreign state of incorporation + the State of its principal place of business = nerve center, where officers direct and control the business (§ 1332(c)(1); Hertz).

front: Citizenship of an LLC or partnership?
back: Every member's citizenship, traced through all layers (Carden). State of organization and principal place of business are irrelevant (outside CAFA).

front: Aggregation rules for amount in controversy?
back: One plaintiff may aggregate all claims against one defendant; multiple plaintiffs may not aggregate separate claims; one plaintiff v. multiple defendants only if jointly liable.
Class action with 100+ members, aggregate amount over $5 million, minimal diversity; local-controversy/home-state exceptions; removal by any defendant without consent (§§ 1332(d), 1453).
Claims so related they form part of the same Article III case — a common nucleus of operative fact (Gibbs).
In diversity-only cases: claims BY PLAINTIFFS against persons joined under Rules 14, 19, 20 or 24, and claims by Rule 19/24 plaintiffs, when inconsistent with § 1332 (Kroger).
In a diversity case, Rule 20 co-plaintiffs and Rule 23 class members below $75,000 may join if one plaintiff satisfies the amount and diversity is complete.

front: Four § 1367(c) grounds to decline supplemental jurisdiction?
back: Novel/complex state issue; state claim substantially predominates; all original-jurisdiction claims dismissed; exceptional circumstances.
If, after removal, the plaintiff amends to drop all federal claims, the federal court loses supplemental jurisdiction over the state claims and must remand (absent another basis).
Only defendants to the plaintiff's claims; to the federal district and division embracing the state court (§ 1441(a)).
A case removable only on diversity cannot be removed if any properly joined and served defendant is a citizen of the forum State (§ 1441(b)(2)); procedural — raise within 30 days.
30 days after formal service (or after other paper shows removability); all properly joined and served defendants must consent; each defendant has its own 30 days (§ 1446(b)).
A diversity case may not be removed more than 1 year after commencement unless the plaintiff acted in bad faith to prevent removal (§ 1446(c)(1)).
Procedural defects: motion within 30 days after notice of removal. Lack of SMJ: any time before final judgment (§ 1447(c)).
Generally no (§ 1447(d)), except in § 1442/§ 1443 removals and CAFA cases by permission.
A court's erroneous dismissal of a properly joined non-diverse defendant after removal does not cure the jurisdictional defect; the judgment must be vacated and the case remanded.
(1) Statutory authority (state long-arm via Rule 4(k)(1)(A)); (2) due process. CCP § 410.10 reaches the constitutional limit.
Personal service while voluntarily present (Burnham); domicile (Milliken); consent; waiver by omitting the defense from the first Rule 12 response.
A State may require out-of-state corporations to consent to general jurisdiction as a condition of registration if the statute expressly says so.

front: Where is a corporation 'at home' for general jurisdiction?
back: Place of incorporation and principal place of business; elsewhere only in an exceptional case (Daimler; BNSF).
(1) Purposeful availment/direction; (2) claim arises out of or relates to the contacts; (3) fair play and substantial justice.

front: Is foreseeability enough for purposeful availment?
back: No. The defendant's own deliberate contacts are required; unilateral acts of others don't count (World-Wide Volkswagen; Hanson).
'Relate to' does not require causation; a company that systematically serves a forum market for a product can be sued there when that product injures a forum resident in the forum.
Non-residents' claims need their own link to the forum; residents' similar claims do not supply it.
Burden on defendant; forum State's interest; plaintiff's interest in convenient relief; interstate efficiency; shared state policy interests. Defendant must make a compelling case.
Asahi: O'Connor requires 'something more' targeting the forum; Brennan accepts regular flow with awareness. Nicastro: single isolated sale insufficient. Argue both.
Intentional conduct expressly aimed at the forum causing known harm there supports PJ; but the plaintiff cannot be the only link — focus on defendant's contacts with the forum itself.
All jurisdiction, including quasi in rem, must satisfy minimum contacts; attaching unrelated property is not enough.
Rule 4(k)(1)(B): parties joined under Rule 14 or 19 may be served within 100 miles of where the summons issued, even across state lines.
Notice reasonably calculated, under all the circumstances, to apprise parties and give them a chance to object; publication insufficient for known addresses.

front: Methods of serving an individual under Rule 4(e)?
back: Personal delivery; leaving at dwelling with person of suitable age and discretion who resides there; authorized agent; or state-law method of forum State or State of service.

front: Who may serve and how long?
back: Any non-party at least 18; within 90 days after filing (Rule 4(c)(2), 4(m)).
Request gives at least 30 days (60 abroad) to return; waiving defendant answers 60 days after request sent (90 abroad); unjustified refusal → service costs. Doesn't waive PJ/venue.

(1) District where any defendant resides if all reside in one State; (2) substantial part of events/omissions or property; (3) fallback: any district where a defendant is subject to PJ, only if no other.

front: Where does an entity defendant reside for venue?
back: Any district where it is subject to PJ for the action (multi-district State: district treated as a State) (§ 1391(c)(2), (d)).
§ 1404: venue proper; convenience transfer; transferor's law follows (Van Dusen/Ferens). § 1406: venue improper; dismiss or transfer; transferee's law (majority).
Valid forum-selection clause enforced by § 1404(a)/FNC; plaintiff's choice gets no weight; private factors drop out; transferor's choice-of-law rules don't follow.
Adequate alternative forum + private and public interest factors strongly favor it; less favorable law not decisive (Piper). CA: CCP § 410.30, stay for residents.
In diversity/supplemental state-law claims, federal courts apply state substantive law and federal procedural law (Erie; RDA § 1652).

front: When does a Federal Rule displace state law?
back: When it is sufficiently broad to answer the question and really regulates procedure under the Rules Enabling Act (Hanna; Shady Grove; Berk v. Choy).
Rule 8 governs what a complaint must contain, so a state affidavit-of-merit requirement does not apply in federal diversity suits; state law's substantive purpose irrelevant.

If no federal rule: would ignoring state law be outcome-determinative so as to encourage forum shopping or inequitable administration (twin aims)? If so apply state law, unless Byrd federal interest outweighs.

front: Which law in diversity: statute of limitations, tolling, choice of law?
back: State law (York; Walker); forum State's choice-of-law rules (Klaxon).
Uniquely federal interests + significant conflict: U.S. commercial paper (Clearfield), contractor defense (Boyle), interstate water/pollution, foreign relations, admiralty, LMRA § 301.
Likely success on merits; likely irreparable harm; balance of equities; public interest. Notice required.

front: TRO without notice — requirements and duration?
back: Specific facts in affidavit/verified complaint showing immediate irreparable injury + attorney certification of notice efforts; max 14 days, one extension; dissolve on 2 days' notice.
Factual content allowing a reasonable inference of liability — plausible, not conceivable; disregard legal conclusions.
Fraud or mistake pleaded with particularity (who, what, when, where, how); intent and knowledge may be alleged generally.
21 days after service; 60 days after waiver request sent; 14 days after ruling on a Rule 12 motion (Rule 12(a)).

front: Which Rule 12 defenses are waived if omitted from the first Rule 12 motion?
back: Lack of PJ, improper venue, insufficient process, insufficient service (12(h)(1)).

front: When can failure to state a claim and failure to join a Rule 19 party be raised?
back: In any pleading, by 12(c) motion, or at trial (12(h)(2)). SMJ any time (12(h)(3)).
Once, within 21 days after serving, or 21 days after service of responsive pleading or 12(b)/(e)/(f) motion, whichever earlier; otherwise consent or leave freely given (Foman).

front: Relation back of a new defendant?
back: Same conduct/transaction + within 90 days new party had notice (no prejudice) and knew or should have known it would have been sued but for a mistake (Rule 15(c)(1)(C); Krupski).
Not for improper purpose; legal contentions warranted; factual contentions have (or likely will have) evidentiary support; denials warranted — after reasonable inquiry.
Motion served but not filed until 21 days later, only if the paper is not withdrawn or corrected (Rule 11(c)(2)).
Limited to deterrence; no monetary sanctions on represented party for frivolous legal contentions; court-initiated monetary sanctions need OSC before dismissal/settlement.
Arises out of same transaction/occurrence as opposing party's claim and needs no party beyond the court's jurisdiction; omitted → barred (Rule 13(a)).
No. Crossclaims against coparties (same transaction or property) are always permissive (Rule 13(g)).
Right to relief jointly, severally or alternatively from the same transaction/occurrence/series + a common question of law or fact.
Complete relief impossible without them; or their interest may be impaired; or existing party faces risk of inconsistent obligations.
No (Temple v. Synthes) — merely permissive.
Prejudice; ways to reduce it; adequacy of judgment without the person; plaintiff's alternative remedy — equity and good conscience.
Defending party may bring in a nonparty who is or may be liable to it for all or part of the claim (derivative liability); no leave within 14 days after serving original answer.
Timely motion + interest in the subject + practical impairment + inadequate representation by existing parties (Rule 24(a)(2)).
Statutory: $500+, minimal diversity among claimants, nationwide service, deposit. Rule 22: ordinary SMJ (complete diversity, > $75,000), ordinary PJ and venue.
Numerosity, commonality (common contention resolvable in one stroke — Dukes), typicality, adequacy.

Common questions predominate + class action superior; best practicable notice incl. individual notice to identifiable members; right to opt out; plaintiff ordinarily pays (court may have D do cheaper tasks such as identifying members).
Court of appeals may permit an appeal of an order granting or denying class certification if the petition is filed within 14 days.
Witnesses and documents the party may use to support its claims or defenses; damages computation; insurance; within 14 days after the 26(f) conference.
Opinions + basis; facts/data considered; exhibits; qualifications incl. publications in prior 10 years; cases testified in prior 4 years; compensation. Due 90 days before trial.
Nonprivileged matter relevant to any party's claim or defense and proportional to the needs of the case; admissibility not required (Rule 26(b)(1)).
Importance of issues; amount in controversy; relative access to information; parties' resources; importance of discovery; burden/expense vs. benefit.
Withholding party must expressly claim privilege and describe withheld items enough to assess the claim (26(b)(5)(A)); since Dec. 1, 2025 the 26(f) plan and 16(b) order address log timing and method.

Documents prepared in anticipation of litigation by or for a party/representative — discoverable only on substantial need + inability to obtain substantial equivalent without undue hardship (Hickman).
Mental impressions, conclusions, opinions, legal theories of attorney or representative — near-absolute protection (26(b)(3)(B)).
Only under Rule 35(b) or on exceptional circumstances making it impracticable to obtain the facts/opinions otherwise (26(b)(4)(D)).
10 per side; one deposition per deponent; one day of 7 hours — without leave or stipulation (Rule 30).

front: When can a non-party witness's deposition be used at trial?
back: Witness dead; more than 100 miles away or abroad (unless procured); age, illness, infirmity, imprisonment; unavailable by subpoena; exceptional circumstances (Rule 32(a)(4)).
25 including discrete subparts; parties only; answer within 30 days (Rule 33).
Deemed admitted after 30 days; withdrawal only if it promotes merits and no prejudice (Rule 36).
Motion; good cause; party's physical or mental condition in controversy; court order specifying terms; licensed examiner (Schlagenhauf).
Prejudice → measures no greater than necessary; intent to deprive → adverse presumption/instruction, dismissal or default.
Good cause to protect from annoyance, embarrassment, oppression, undue burden or expense + certification of good-faith conferral (Rule 26(c)).

front: Expenses on a granted motion to compel?
back: Mandatory unless movant failed to confer first, opposition substantially justified, or award unjust (Rule 37(a)(5)).
Facts established; preclusion; striking pleadings; stay; dismissal; default judgment; contempt (not for Rule 35 order).
Before opposing party serves answer or SJ motion; without prejudice unless plaintiff previously dismissed the same claim (two-dismissal rule) (Rule 41(a)(1)).
Adjudication on the merits unless order says otherwise, except dismissals for jurisdiction, venue or Rule 19.
Clerk only for sum certain against non-appearing competent adult; 7 days' notice to party who appeared; cannot differ in kind or exceed amount demanded (Rule 54(c)).
In MDL proceedings the transferee court should hold an initial management conference and may order a pre-conference report; flexible framework.
Jury right for 'suits at common law' — compare to 1791 actions and, more importantly, ask if the remedy is legal (damages) or equitable.

front: Mixed legal and equitable claims sharing facts?
back: Jury decides legal claims and common issues first (Beacon Theatres; Dairy Queen).
Serve within 14 days after the last pleading directed to the issue; otherwise waived (court may still allow under Rule 39(b)).

front: Federal civil jury size and unanimity?
back: 6 to 12 jurors; unanimous verdict by at least 6 unless parties stipulate otherwise (Rule 48).

front: Peremptory challenges in federal civil trials?
back: Three per party (28 U.S.C. § 1870); Batson applies to civil litigants (Edmonson).
Object on the record, stating distinctly the matter and grounds, before instructions are given; otherwise plain error only (Rule 51).
If matters outside the pleadings are presented on 12(b)(6) or 12(c) and not excluded, the motion becomes summary judgment with opportunity to respond.
No genuine dispute as to any material fact and movant entitled to judgment as a matter of law; genuine = reasonable jury could find for non-movant (Anderson).
Movant without trial burden may point to absence of evidence; non-movant must cite specific admissible record evidence showing a genuine dispute.
After party fully heard, no legally sufficient evidentiary basis for a reasonable jury to find for it; evidence viewed for non-movant; no credibility weighing (Rule 50(a); Reeves).
Prior Rule 50(a) motion on same grounds; filed within 28 days after judgment; may join new-trial request; no extensions (Unitherm).
Clear weight of evidence, excessive/inadequate damages, legal error, misconduct, new evidence; within 28 days after judgment; judge may weigh evidence (Rule 59).

front: Remittitur vs. additur in federal court?
back: Remittitur allowed (new trial unless plaintiff accepts reduction); additur forbidden by Seventh Amendment (Dimick).
(1) mistake/excusable neglect, (2) new evidence, (3) fraud/misconduct — within reasonable time and ≤ 1 year; (4) void, (5) satisfied/changed, (6) other — reasonable time.
A Rule 60(b)(4) motion attacking a void judgment is subject to the Rule 60(c)(1) reasonable-time limit.

front: Inconsistent general verdict and answers (answers consistent with each other)?
back: Court may enter judgment on the answers, return jury for further consideration, or order new trial (Rule 49(b)(3)).
Juror failed to answer honestly a material voir dire question, and a correct answer would have provided a valid basis for a challenge for cause.
Same claim (transactional test, Restatement § 24); same parties or privies; valid final judgment on the merits.
Same issue; actually litigated and determined; valid final judgment; essential to the judgment; party bound had full and fair opportunity.

front: Parklane factors for offensive non-mutual issue preclusion?
back: Plaintiff could easily have joined earlier; defendant's incentive to litigate; inconsistent prior judgments; procedural opportunities unavailable earlier.

front: When is a non-party bound (Taylor v. Sturgell)?
back: Agreement; substantive legal relationship; adequate representation (class, fiduciary); control of prior suit; proxy; special statutory scheme. No 'virtual representation'.

front: Preclusive effect of a federal diversity judgment?
back: Federal common law adopting the law of the State where the federal court sat, unless incompatible with federal interests (Semtek).

front: Final judgment rule and notice of appeal deadline?
back: § 1291: appeal from final decisions; notice within 30 days after entry (60 if U.S. party); tolled by timely 50(b), 52(b), 59, early 60 motions.
With multiple claims/parties, court may enter final judgment on fewer than all only on express determination of no just reason for delay.
Controlling question of law + substantial ground for difference of opinion + immediate appeal may materially advance termination; apply to court of appeals within 10 days.
Order conclusively determines disputed question, resolves important issue separate from the merits, and is effectively unreviewable after final judgment (Cohen).

front: Are privilege-disclosure orders or derivative sovereign immunity denials collateral orders?
back: No (Mohawk; GEO Group v. Menocal (2026)).
Amount in controversy $35,000 or less (exclusive of fees, interest, costs) (CCP § 85); restricted discovery; appeal to appellate division.

front: California response time and PJ challenge?
back: 30 days after service; challenge PJ/service by motion to quash on or before last day to plead (CCP § 418.10) — general appearance waives.
After reasonable diligence at personal service: leave at home with competent household member 18+ or office with person in charge, then mail; complete 10 days after mailing (CCP § 415.20).
County where any defendant resides; for personal injury also where injury occurred; contracts also where made or to be performed (CCP § 395).

front: California pleading standard and general demurrer?
back: Fact pleading: facts constituting the cause of action (CCP § 425.10). General demurrer: failure to state facts sufficient (never waived); special demurrers (e.g., uncertainty) waived if not raised. Fraud must be pleaded with particularity (Lazar).
Plaintiff genuinely ignorant of defendant's identity may sue a Doe and later substitute the true name with relation back (CCP § 474).
Mistake, inadvertence, surprise or excusable neglect — within reasonable time not exceeding 6 months; mandatory if attorney's sworn affidavit of fault (CCP § 473(b)).
(1) Defendant shows claim arises from protected speech/petition activity (§ 425.16(e)); (2) plaintiff must show probability of prevailing (legally sufficient + prima facie evidence).
Motion within 60 days of service; discovery stayed; prevailing defendant gets fees; order appealable (§ 904.1(a)(13)).
Defendant who answers must cross-complain on any related cause of action (same transaction) it has against the plaintiff or lose it (CCP § 426.30).
Relevant to the subject matter + admissible or reasonably calculated to lead to admissible evidence (CCP § 2017.010) — broader than federal.
35 specially prepared interrogatories; 35 RFAs (except genuineness of documents); unlimited inspection demands; motion to compel further responses within 45 days.

front: California physical exam of personal-injury plaintiff?
back: Defendant may demand one exam without court order if not painful/protracted/intrusive and within 75 miles of plaintiff's residence; mental exam requires leave and good cause.
Only on demand of a party; due within 60 days of the demand; some actions exempt (CCP § 2016.090).
$1,000 for specified misconduct, e.g., failing to respond in good faith to a document request or to meet and confer in good faith (CCP § 2023.050).

Attorney's impressions, conclusions, opinions, research or theories absolutely protected; other work product qualified (unfair prejudice/injustice); belongs to attorney; witness statements protected (Coito).
Notice 81 days before hearing; opposition 20 days; reply 11 days; hearing at least 30 days before trial; separate statement required (CCP § 437c).
Only if it completely disposes of a cause of action, affirmative defense, punitive-damages claim, or issue of duty (§ 437c(f)(1)).
A cause of action is defined by the primary right invaded (the harm), not the legal theory; one injury = one cause of action (Slater; Mycogen).

front: Is a California judgment final for preclusion while on appeal?
back: No — not until the appeal is exhausted or the time to appeal expires (Samara; CCP § 1049). Federal majority: final when entered.

front: California civil jury verdict and size?
back: Three-fourths of the jury (e.g., 9 of 12); 12 jurors unless parties agree to fewer (Cal. Const. art. I, § 16); right as at common law in 1850.
Granted whenever a directed verdict should have been granted had a motion been made — no prior directed-verdict motion required (CCP § 629).
Notice of intention within 15 days after service of notice of entry of judgment or 180 days after entry; court must rule within 75 days or motion denied (CCP §§ 659, 660).

front: California appeal deadline and route for non-appealable orders?
back: 60 days after service of notice of entry (180 days after entry if none); writ of mandate/prohibition for interlocutory rulings like SJ denials (20 days).
California's Rule 11: certification after reasonable inquiry; 21-day safe harbor; deterrence-limited sanctions.
Ordinary waiver principles — conduct inconsistent with the right; no prejudice requirement (also federal: Morgan v. Sundance).
